posts.text: Missing access control lets an unintended account call privileged functions.
Permissions are missing or applied inconsistently across privileged entry points, creating the gap.
Different privileged operations can require different roles.
Mitigate by defining roles explicitly and testing unauthorized calls for every privileged operation.
How will you verify that role assignment and removal, which are permission-sensitive operations, are correctly restricted?
Missing access control lets anyone call privileged functions. A sensitive function without adequate authorization can be called by an unintended account.
The root cause is missing or inconsistently applied permissions across privileged entry points, allowing unintended callers to execute critical logic.
Different privileged operations can require different roles, so a single missing check may expose several functions.
Mitigate by defining roles explicitly and testing unauthorized calls for every privileged operation.
How will you verify that role assignment and revocation themselves are permission-sensitive and correctly restricted?
